Reasoning: The target word is KANGAROO, and the corresponding positions are K, A, N, G, A, R, O, O. Compare the current positions O, A, R, G, O, N, K, A with the target positions K, A, N, G, A, R, O, O: the 2nd position A and the 4th position G are already correct; the 1st, 3rd, 5th, 6th, 7th, and 8th positions are incorrect, for a total of 6 incorrect positions. One swap can correct at most two incorrect positions, so at least 6/2 = 3 swaps are needed. 3 swaps are indeed enough: swap the 1st position and the 7th position to get K A R G O N O A; swap the 3rd position and the 6th position to get K A N G O R O A; swap the 5th position and the 8th position to get K A N G A R O O. Therefore the minimum needed is 3 moves.

method.method_draft: Read the cards in the image from left to right as O A R G O N K A, and read the text target word as KANGAROO. Compare each position with K A N G A R O O: positions 2 and 4 are already correct, while positions 1, 3, 5, 6, 7, and 8 are wrong. Since one swap can correct at most two wrong positions, at least 6/2 = 3 swaps are needed. Then show 3 swaps suffice: swap positions 1 and 7 to put K first and O seventh; swap positions 3 and 6 to put N third and R sixth; swap positions 5 and 8 to put A fifth and O eighth. This reaches KANGAROO, so the minimum is 3.
